title: Elastic reservation swap and commitment rebalancer
creator: Ava Ramirez
description:
Problem: Customers with multiple reserved pools (for product teams or environments) frequently need to reallocate committed throughput when usage patterns shift (e.g., marketing campaign spikes, model rollout testing, or cross-team project reassignments). Today this requires manual ops + billing adjustments which is slow, error-prone, and leads to either wasted committed capacity or missed SLAs.

Proposal: Implement an Elastic Reservation Swap feature together with a Commitment Rebalancer service and an approval workflow in the console/API. Core abilities:
- Allow customers to propose a transfer of reserved throughput between two existing reservations (within the same org and billing account).
- Provide instant pre-checks (quota, compatibility, model/region affinity) and a cost delta preview before approval.
- Support automatic rebalancing recommendations from the Capacity Planner based on recent utilization and forecasted demand.
- Wire in an approvals lane (self-approve for same-owner transfers; 2-step approvals for cross-team transfers) with configurable guardrails.
- Integrate with billing to prorate commitments and with fleet controls to move dedicated capacity slices without disrupting running serving instances.

Why this matters: Improves reservation utilization, reduces ops overhead for customers, and lowers the need for conservative over-provisioning. It also surfaces a new upsell surface (temporary top-ups, swap fee tiers) and tightens our Dedicated product fit for customers with variable workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Console: users can initiate a reservation swap with source and target reservations selectable and a live pre-check report shown
API: POST /v1/dedicated/reservations/swap returns a staged transaction id and preflight result
Approval: transactions respect org-level approval policy; self-transfers auto-approve, cross-team transfers create approval task
Billing: billing system receives swap event and returns accurate prorated charge/credit preview
Fleet: rebalancer executes capacity reallocation within 10 minutes without dropping existing SLO-backed requests (best-effort); fallback to rolling rollback on failure
Observability: new metrics for swap_attempts, swap_success_rate, swap_latency and swap_impact_estimate emitted to Console and Alerting
Security: all operations are audited and traceable with the requestor, approver, and transaction id
implementation_notes: Introduce Commitment Rebalancer microservice (stateless coordinator + orchestrator) that talks to Fleet Controller and Billing API
New DB table: reservation_swap_transactions with states [staged, pending_approval, executing, complete, failed, rolled_back]
Console flow: 'Propose swap' modal shows utilization graphs (last 30d), forecast delta (Capacity Planner), and cost delta. Modal links to approval rules and change history
API contract: POST /v1/dedicated/reservations/swap { source_reservation_id, target_reservation_id, throughput_units, effective_time }
Rollback strategy: snapshot current allocation + ordered move plan. If a host move step errors, pause and try canonical fallback (drain then migrate) before reversing changes
Autoscaling interplay: swaps must not reduce a reservation below its current min_sla floor; autoscale policies may temporarily lift to maintain request-level SLOs during move
decision_log: Trade-off: synchronous vs. asynchronous swap execution — chose asynchronous orchestration (staged + job queue) to avoid long API timeouts and allow human approvals
Trade-off: full live migration vs. allocation pointer flip — initial MVP uses allocation pointer flip when possible to minimize data movement; full live eviction/migrate planned for v2
Policy: only allow swaps within same billing account for MVP to avoid cross-billing reconciliation complexity

qa_plan: Unit and integration tests for transaction state machine (staged -> executing -> complete -> rolled_back)
End-to-end test: create two reservations in staging org, propose 50% swap, approve, verify billing delta and fleet allocations
Chaos test: while swap executes, inject node failures and validate rollback correctness
Performance test: run 100 parallel swap requests in staging to validate queueing/backpressure behavior
observability_requirements: Emit swap_transaction_id on all related logs and traces
Console dashboard: per-org swap history timeline and impact heatmap
Alerts: swap_failure_rate > 5% over 1h => paging to SRE oncall
rollback_plan: If executing rebalancer detects a violation (quota, region mismatch, or node failure), it should pause the job, attempt two retry windows with exponential backoff, and then perform an automated rollback applying the snapshot plan. If rollback fails, create an incident with priority P0 and provide a manual remediation runbook to SRE.
cost_estimate: Engineering: ~6-8 sprint points across Eng and Infra; Billing work: 2-3 points; Design: 2 points. Total FY26-Q2 cost estimated at ~1.5 FTE-months to deliver MVP
